accuracy.evidence: Checked 612 against AQA A-level Chemistry 3.1.6.1 (at equilibrium forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates; concentrations of reactants and products remain constant), OCR A 3.2.3 (dynamic equilibrium in a closed system) and NGSS HS-PS1-6. Lab model is A ⇌ B with first-order steps: rate_f = kf[A], rate_b = kb[B], so [B]/[A] = kf/kb; with kf 0.6 and kb 0.4 s⁻¹ the mix is 60% B from either side, rates equal 0.24 at 4.5 s as shown. Hydrated copper sulfate dehydration in an open tube is described as reversible but not at equilibrium. Items checked: m8 0.6:0.4 = 60%, m3 kf = kb[B]/[A].

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented A-level equilibrium misconceptions (e.g. Hackling & Garnett; Banerjee): reactions stop at equilibrium, equal rates mean equal concentrations (50:50), the forward reaction finishes before the reverse starts, the starting side changes the equilibrium mix, and ignoring the closed-system condition (open flask step and copper sulfate item).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagequil simulates particles flipping between A and B with rate constants, a rates-vs-time cursor, a run from the opposite side, a tracer particle and an escaping-gas open flask; no other flag lab models reversible kinetics (flagcoll is collision theory, flagredox electron transfer). Lab gate shingle overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the amounts level off while green flashes show reactions continuing, finds by dragging that the rate curves meet where amounts go flat (at 60:40, not 50:50), gets the same 60% from all B, watches a tagged particle flip A → B → A at steady totals, and makes the reaction go to completion by opening the flask; the sandbox shows kf and kb set the position.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'both have stopped' (step 1), 'always equal' amounts (rates step), 'stays all B' / 'the reverse 40%' (start from B), 'no: the reaction has stopped' (tracer), and 'a new 60% B mix forms' (open flask).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Rotating questions on rates, concentrations, the closed system and a generated %B from kf and kb. Each wrong option has its own message: 'stop' (reactions continue at equal rates), 'one' (a faster forward rate would keep B rising), 'equal' (constant is not equal), 'swap' (uses kf[A] = kb[B] with the actual numbers), 'open' (gas escapes, goes to completion).

readability.evidence: Learner kid text FK grade 3.2 and adult 8.5 (targets 6.5 and 9.5). Uses the A-level terms precisely: reversible reaction, ⇌, forward and backward (reverse) reaction, rate, closed system, dynamic equilibrium, concentration, rate constant, equilibrium position.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean. Kid paragraphs walk through the ⇌ idea, the changing rates, the equal-rate state and the closed-system condition; adult paragraphs give the specification points, the kf[A] = kb[B] reasoning and copper sulfate example, four named mistakes, and the lab steps.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (dark and light) after each Show me and on desktop: flask above graph on phones, particle legend in particle colours, rate readout and cursor line legible, open-lid label beside the lid, buttons below the canvas; nothing clipped or overlapping after moving the message line clear of the lid.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Run/Pause, Earlier/Later for the time line, Tag a particle, Open/Close the flask, kf/kb up and down, Restart; the canvas aria-label carries each message; walk.cjs axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: AQA AS and A-level Chemistry specification 7404/7405, 3.1.6.1 Chemical equilibria and Le Chatelier's principle
OCR A-level Chemistry A H432, 3.2.3 Chemical equilibrium (dynamic equilibrium in a closed system)
NGSS HS-PS1-6; Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry: first-order opposing reactions A ⇌ B, K = kf/kb
RSC Education, 'Chemical misconceptions: prevention, diagnosis and cure' (Keith Taber), equilibrium misconceptions
